title: Meet The Cartozians by Talene Monahon at Second Stage #meetthecartozi...
transcript: I love when a play is heady but still very entertaining, and that is precisely the brilliance of Meet The Cartozians by Talene Monahon. In a way, it's two plays in conversation with one another. Act 1 focuses on an Armenian American family seeking US citizenship in 1923, and Act 2 takes place a hundred years later with a very different group of Armenian Americans. We see how in just a century, racial lines can move and culture can become costume. It's about how our relationship to our heritage and culture can change over time, while illustrating how these conversations around race and identity were sticky then and sticky now. This play is packed with ideas — it brings up colorism and proximity to whiteness, how it's weaponized, how it's leveraged, assimilation, citizenship, and immigration. But while the themes are heavy handed, the questions are expansive and the discourse is riveting, especially in Act 2 — it's also quite funny and satirical. Will Brill and Andrea Martin are notably hilarious, but everyone in the cast is fantastic and giving impressive double performances. All in all, I learned, I laughed, and I have much to chew on — a great theatrical experience, Pulitzer material, in my book. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
